title: 1 Kings 5
paragraphs: ¹ When Hiram king of Tyre heard that Solomon had been anointed king in place of his father David, he sent his envoys to Solomon, because Hiram had always been on friendly terms with David. ² Solomon sent back this message to Hiram: ³ "You know that my father David was unable to build a temple for the name of the LORD his God because of the wars waged against him on all sides, until the LORD put his enemies under his feet. ⁴ But now the LORD my God has given me rest on every side, with no adversary and no misfortune. ⁵ I intend to build a temple for the name of the LORD my God, just as the LORD told my father David when he said: 'Your son, whom I will put on your throne in your place, will build the temple for my name.'"

⁶ "So now give orders to have cedar logs cut for me from Lebanon. My workers will work alongside yours, and I will pay your workers whatever rate you set. As you know, we have no one as skilled in felling timber as the Sidonians." ⁷ When Hiram heard Solomon's message, he was very pleased, and said, "Praise the LORD today, for he has given David a wise son to rule over this great nation." ⁸ So Hiram sent Solomon this reply: "I have received your message. I will do everything you want — I will supply you with all the cedar and pine logs you need. ⁹ My men will haul them down from Lebanon to the Mediterranean Sea, and I will float them as rafts to whatever place you specify. There I will have them separated, and you can take them. In return, I ask that you provide food for my household." ¹⁰ So Hiram kept Solomon supplied with as much cedar and pine as he desired.

¹¹ Solomon in turn gave Hiram twenty thousand cors of wheat as food for his household, and twenty cors of pure olive oil. Solomon gave Hiram this amount year by year. ¹² The LORD gave Solomon wisdom, just as he had promised, and there was peaceful relations between Hiram and Solomon, and they made a treaty. ¹³ King Solomon conscripted laborers from all Israel — thirty thousand men in all. ¹⁴ He sent them to Lebanon in shifts of ten thousand a month — one month in Lebanon, two months at home. Adoniram was in charge of the forced labor. ¹⁵ Solomon had seventy thousand men who carried loads and eighty thousand who quarried stone in the hills,

¹⁶ besides three thousand three hundred foremen who supervised the workers. ¹⁷ At the king's command they quarried large blocks of high-quality stone to give the temple a foundation of dressed stone. ¹⁸ The craftsmen of Solomon and Hiram, along with the men of Gebal, cut and prepared the timber and stone for the building of the temple.
